clue.text: Eastern princess enters tree and flower

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the first pair of pieces is placed within the tree

blocks.note: a gum is a eucalyptus tree
standard abbreviation for east
a rani is an Indian princess or queen

explanation.surface: An oriental princess climbs into a tree full of blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: The rani is a Hindu queen or princess; the gum tree is the eucalyptus.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a common garden and pot plant grown for its blooms, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Land with feathers  reduced to powder

blocks.note: ground is earth or land
down is soft fine plumage

explanation.surface: Earth and soft plumage together crumble into dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something milled or crushed until fine has been made into a powder, a past participle phrase matching the clue.

clue.text: Broadcast keeping one in television, it appears - that's the general theory

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the broadcast word holds the rest
one item placed inside another is in it, so the single letter goes within the set

blocks.note: to relay a programme is to broadcast it
common abbreviation
Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something seen on television claims to explain everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the numeral sits inside the television abbreviation, and that plus the next word sits inside the broadcast word. 'It appears' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein published his special theory first and his general theory later, both about relativity, so the famous phrase names this answer.

clue.text: Poor journalist in craving for elevation

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word makes it read from bottom to top
one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a yen is a longing
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A hard-up reporter longs for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevation' turns the craving upward before the journalist is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy and poor are synonyms describing people lacking money and the basic necessities of life.

clue.text: Protecting (everything in the room, say?) from rust

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard, matching another written form by its sound

blocks.note: everything in a room is below its ceiling

explanation.surface: Guarding the contents of a room, it seems, against corrosion.
explanation.walkthrough: Underseal is the protective coating sprayed under a car body against rust; 'from rust' completes the definition rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersealing a car coats its underside, shielding the metal against corrosion, so it is a way of protecting it.

clue.text: Backward writer to cut example of 2?

indicators.note: something backward faces the other way, so that word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to hew is to chop

explanation.surface: A shy author has to trim an illustration of a theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is RELATIVITY; the question mark admits the setter is reading it as 'relative', and a nephew is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a family member, a relative, which the setter teases out of the word relativity at 2-down.

clue.text: Aristocratic girl, possibly, should get 8

definitions.note: a cryptic description; the noun phrase names one who gets the worm

blocks.note: jokingly, like an earl, with 'possibly' admitting the stretch
bird is British slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A posh young lady ought to be rewarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is WORM: the proverb says the early bird catches the worm.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'the early bird catches the worm' means the first to rise wins, so this is who gets it.

clue.text: In Holland it could be slung with 8 on it

definitions.text: In Holland it could be slung

blocks.clueFragment: In Holland it could be slung
blocks.note: the ... of Holland is a Dutch port, and to sling one's ... is British slang for clearing off
8 is WORM: an angler baits this with a worm

explanation.surface: Something in the Netherlands thrown about with bait attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling your hook' is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman's barbed metal curve carries the bait, and the Dutch ferry port bears the same name.

clue.text: Extract information from woman or man, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letters count

blocks.note: first letter
taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: An interrogator pumps a woman or man for facts.
explanation.walkthrough: To worm something out of someone is to get it by persistent questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To worm a secret out of somebody is to draw facts from them gradually and craftily, by persistent probing.

clue.text: Effects of rape - so diesel is produced

indicators.note: something produced is made into a new form, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

blocks.note: fodder

explanation.surface: Crop oil makes biodiesel, so a farmer's harvest fuels engines.
explanation.walkthrough: Rape here is the oilseed rape plant, the yellow-flowered crop; 'effects' means its products.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilseed rape is grown for its seeds, which are crushed for oil, so these are what the crop yields.

clue.text: Use more force, we 'ear, or it'll get cooled

indicators.note: this is how we hear it, with the dropped h of a Cockney accent signalling sound over spelling

blocks.note: push harder, with the h dropped

explanation.surface: Press on harder, or your enthusiasm will cool off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, 'harder' without its h sounds like this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passion or burning enthusiasm, which proverbially cools over time, so it is the thing that gets cooled.

clue.text: Aside from male, we got upset when his agent turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting a word tips it over so it reads from the bottom
turning something up in a down entry flips it so the word reads upward

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
taken as written
taken as written
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: We were annoyed when this man's agent arrived unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark an actor makes to the audience, meant to be heard but supposedly unheard by others on stage.

clue.text: The lousy, dirty 24s

blocks.note: literally, full of nits or lice
covered in grit

explanation.surface: Dirty, lice-ridden particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the nitty-gritty means tackling the basic practical specifics of a matter, its essential particulars.

clue.text: They may be linked and shot

blocks.note: fastened with cufflinks
to shoot one's cuffs is to pull them out beyond a jacket sleeve

explanation.surface: Things that are connected and then fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The ends of shirt sleeves are fastened with links and are pulled forward, or shot, by a dapper wearer.

clue.text: 24s for descendants and supporters - lots

definitions.note: the details that those getting down get down to

blocks.note: a bra supports
stacks means a great many

explanation.surface: Many details are left to heirs and their backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is DETAIL. 'Get down to brass tacks' means tackle the details, so 'descendants' are those getting down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom getting down to brass tacks means turning to essential practical facts, so these are what one gets down to.

clue.text: Cook in the 24?

blocks.note: to ... food is to cook it with hot spices
24 is DETAIL: the proverb says the ... is in the detail

explanation.surface: A chef at work on the particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilled kidneys are spicily grilled, and the saying claims the troublemaker hides in small particulars.

clue.text: Let horrid characters be put in charge of broadcasting once

indicators.note: letters that are put somewhere are set down afresh, so their order is changed

blocks.note: fodder

explanation.surface: Nasty types are allowed to run the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded and ran the BBC in its early decades, so he was the historic head of British radio.

clue.text: Sassenach like Chapman or Fitzgerald, maybe single lady

blocks.note: Scots word for an English person
Chapman translated Homer and Fitzgerald Omar Khayyam into English
Elizabeth I, the unmarried queen

explanation.surface: A Scot's view of an English spinster with literary pretensions.
explanation.walkthrough: A third reading: ENGLISH plus ER, the royal cipher, makes an English queen, and Elizabeth I never married.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who renders foreign verse into English is a translator, and Scots also call an English person by this name.

clue.text: Current turns falter, interrupting great success

indicators.note: something that turns changes its position, so these letters are rearranged
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: a wow is a hit
fodder

explanation.surface: Momentum stutters, cutting short a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a stream moving in one direction, which is how liquid moves in a river or a pipe.

clue.text: Beetle is female from Greece

blocks.note: the dor is a dung beetle
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect is a Greek woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris was the region of the ancient Dorians, and the Greek name Doris originally meant a woman of that people.

clue.text: The Pobble's aunt's pet, given by Bantu cleric

indicators.note: a thing given by someone is handed over in their own new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: fodder

explanation.surface: An African priest presents a nonsense animal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem The Pobble Who Has No Toes, Aunt Jobiska owns a Runcible Cat with crimson whiskers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's nonsense verse gives the Pobble an Aunt Jobiska whose animal companion has crimson whiskers.

clue.text: See with temp

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look
Latin for with, as in 'kitchen-cum-dining room'

explanation.surface: An office instruction to look at the stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum stands in for a doctor or cleric while they are away, which is temporary work.

clue.text: River in our garden

blocks.note: the ... flows through Cumbria in north-west England
the biblical garden of Adam and Eve, humanity's first home

explanation.surface: A stream runs through the back yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis places the first humans in a paradise garden, and a north English waterway carries the same name.

clue.text: 24 I came across on the way up

indicators.note: in a down entry going upward means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A particular I bumped into while climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single point or particular in a list, the same as a detail.

clue.text: Particular stump

blocks.note: as a noun, an individual point
read as ..., a tail cut to a stump

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical: to de-tail an animal is to dock its tail to a stump.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single fact or item of information; docking a tail leaves a stump.

clue.text: 24, if in charge on the off chance

definitions.note: read as the adjective particular, the clue at 24

blocks.note: doing something on spec means on the off chance
taken as written
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Details, if you are the boss, left to chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the clue to 24, 'Particular', as an adjective rather than DETAIL itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific and particular are adjectives meaning precise and clearly identified rather than general.

clue.text: One seeking to be laid by corporal in play, first in playhouse

blocks.note: Corporal Nym appears in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor
the opening letter of play, then HO, the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: An actor hopes for a fling with a soldier in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The playhouse splits as play plus house: only the first letter of play is kept, and house shrinks to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a woman with a voracious sexual appetite, always looking for a partner in bed.

clue.text: Propositions in or around the house

blocks.note: statements from which an argument proceeds
in a building or its grounds

explanation.surface: Offers made at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical premises are statements assumed in an argument, while a property and its land are a building's premises.
